..
Issued at 251 AM EDT Fri Aug 7 2026

Early morning GOES water vapor features midlevel troughing over 
central Canada and the Northern Plains, extending from a broad 
midlevel low spinning around Hudson Bay. An embedded shortwave is 
moving into far western Ontario, with an associated cold front 
draped southwestward across NW MN and into the Dakotas. Closer to 
home, we remain under a tightening pressure gradient that has 
allowed for breezy SSW winds over the western half of the UP. Skies 
are so far mostly clear, with temperatures only falling back into the 
lower/mid 60s so far. Expect temperatures to bottom out a couple 
degrees cooler, into the upper 50s and lower 60s for most. Nighttime 
microphysics is hinting at some patchy fog development over 
northeastern WI already, so will not rule this out over the eastern 
half of the UP, but increasing winds should keep this patchy and low-
impact. Heading into the daytime hours, expect southerly wind gusts 
to pick up across the rest of the area, while temperatures rebound 
into the lower to mid 80s for most. 

The frontal boundary finally makes its way through the UP later 
today. While 0-6 km bulk shear isn't all that impressive along the 
cold front (only around 30 kts), with models trending the cap weaker 
at around 850mb, convection could become sfc-based by the afternoon 
hours. Thus, we may see SBCAPE/MUCAPE at around 1200 to 1500 J/kg by 
the afternoon to early evening hours over the west half. In 
addition, with strong theta-e advection lined up well with cold 
frontogenesis in the lower to mid levels, thinking there will be 
robust mechanical lift along the front to produce strong updrafts to 
support linear convection Friday afternoon. This is generally 
supported by the varying CAMs; while there is still a range on the 
timing, the general model consensus is that showers and storms move 
in during the mid-afternoon hours (2-4 PM EDT). Thus, while 
generally not expected along the line, a strong thunderstorm or two 
could bring some marginally severe winds (i.e. up to 60 mph) to the 
sfc over the west half this afternoon into early evening; thus, the 
Marginal Risk (category 1 of 5) that SPC has over us. In addition to 
the potentially stronger winds via the convection, some heavy 
rainfall is expected given the robust lift along the front. With 
PWATs generally getting up to around 1.50 inches ahead of the cold 
front, some heavy rainfall in excess of 1 inch could be seen across 
some spots of Upper Michigan; as of the time of this writing, 
ensembles show up to a 50% chance that over an inch of rainfall 
between this afternoon and Saturday morning, with the highest 
chances over the west and north central. Looking at the LPMM for the 
REFS, the expected rainfall ranges from a quarter inch to 2+ inches 
over the west and north central, with the Porkies seeing 4+ inches. 
Therefore, while not expected, there could some spots, especially in 
the west, where some ponding of water/flash flood could occur. 
Across the rest of the U.P., expect generally a tenth of an inch up 
to potentially a whole inch of liquid by Saturday morning.

Moving into the rest of the forecast period, expect generally 
pleasant temperatures with highs in the 70s as a somewhat more zonal 
to northwesterly flow sets up across the Upper Great Lakes. While 
some weak sfc ridging generally sets up across the area, some weak 
shortwaves from time to time look to bring additional showers and 
thunderstorms to the area this weekend through next week. With 850mb 
temperatures dropping to around 9 to 10C behind the cold front early 
on Saturday, we may see some lake effect clouds over the northwest 
wind belts early Saturday morning, before warming temperatures bring 
an end to the cloud cover. Looking at just the 0-6 km bulk shear and 
MUCAPE, there is a chance that we could see some stronger storms 
come Sunday, but confidence on this is very low at this time (<5% 
chance). In addition, with a shortwave low on Monday having trended 
further south and now bringing the wrap-around moisture over the 
U.P., we could see at least a wetting rainfall across the area then 
(the NBM shows a 10 to 60% chance for at least a quarter inch of 
rainfall on Monday). By around next Thursday, we could see some lake 
effect clouds return as strong CAA with 850mb temperatures down to 
6C potentially drop across Lake Superior.
